clue.text: Captain maybe turning vehicle to change direction

indicators.note: a vehicle that is turning round faces the other way, so its word is read backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
to alter is to change
N, north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: An army captain swings a lorry round in the road to head the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses BUS to give SUB. A subaltern is a junior army officer; the setter offers a captain as one such officer, hence 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Subaltern is the general term for a junior commissioned officer in the British Army, a class the setter stretches to take in a captain.

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of, sitting inside, the long bird-order name

explanation.surface: A distinguishing feature of the songbird order.
explanation.walkthrough: Passeriformes is the order of perching birds; its letters pasSERIFormes contain the answer. 'Typical' here means typographic, about type, not characteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke finishing a letter in print, a mark of type.

parts.note: in the game of bowls a bowl is called a wood
to egg on is to spur, so spurred is egged

explanation.surface: Timber urged on by a group of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bandy' is the adjective, as in bandy legs, not the verb to bandy words.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandy legs curve outward at the knee, the shape also called bow-legged.

clue.text: Like Wordsworth's cloud, he's awfully near, without being more extended

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: something more extended is longer

indicators.note: awfully suggests the word near is badly arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A poetic musing on Wordsworth's solitary cloud and a figure lurking close by without growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' signals the anagram and 'without' is its old sense of outside. Wordsworth 'wandered lonely as a cloud'; the definition reads 'he's like that cloud', a solitary figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The masked cowboy hero of radio and film rode alone, like the lonely cloud in Wordsworth's poem.

definitions.meaning: a deposit given as a token that a bargain will be kept

explanation.surface: A promise given as a token of good faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest money is a pledge paid to bind a bargain, and being in earnest means acting with sincerity.

definitions.note: the possessive stands for a golfer's club, so the definition is a noun

parts.note: the nib is the writing point of a pen, standing for it
to lick is to touch with the mouth

explanation.surface: Does a golfer chew the end of a pen while keeping score?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bare possessive: read it as 'a golfer's [club]'. A niblick is an old name for a lofted iron, roughly a nine-iron.
explanation.definitionFit: The niblick was an old wooden-shafted iron club carried in a golf bag.

definitions.meaning: a writer, here the novelist Henry ...
a cue to the catchphrase said to a driver when it is time to head back

explanation.surface: A writer heads back to his house.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James was an American-born novelist, and 'Home, James!' is the stock order to a chauffeur to drive back.

definitions.meaning: a vessel, here a Chinese sailing ship
old objects; the question mark warns they may be rubbish rather than treasures

explanation.surface: A vessel used for carrying antiques.
explanation.definitionFit: A junk is a flat-bottomed Chinese sailing vessel, and junk is also old odds and ends, which the question mark offers as a cheeky name for antiques.

clue.text: It's low church to loiter aimlessly

parts.note: to low is the sound cattle make, a moo

explanation.surface: Low Church Anglicans are mocked for drifting about without purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low church' reads as one churchmanship term, but 'low' is the cow's verb and 'church' a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to wander about idly with no particular purpose.

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
Robert Burns is the Scottish national poet; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A team's poet puts on a bold, impudent show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheeky' means on the cheeks, not impudent.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiskers grown down the side of the face are on show on the cheeks.

indicators.note: backed means the word gold's heraldic name is written from right to left

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
wan means pale

explanation.surface: A golden colour set against pale ash-wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns OR into RO. The mountain ash is another name for the rowan tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan is the mountain ash, a tree of the rose family with ash-like leaves.

clue.text: Rubbish container at house put in back door by outlaw

indicators.note: put in signals one group of letters set inside another
back tells us to read the word door from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a bin holds rubbish

explanation.surface: An outlaw stashes a dustbin from the house behind the back door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses DOOR to ROOD, and BIN plus HO is 'put in' it: RO-BINHO-OD.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary archer of Sherwood Forest was an outlaw who robbed the rich.

clue.text: Desire full effect of French charge

indicators.note: to effect is to bring about, so the letters are worked into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A longing for the full impact of a French accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effect' is the anagram signal on DESIRE FULL. A charge in heraldry is a device shown on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: The stylised lily is the heraldic emblem of the French royal arms, a charge borne on shields.

indicators.note: bottomless means the word loses its last letter, the bottom of a down entry

parts.note: Chubb is a well-known British make of lock

explanation.surface: A fish trapped in a lock with no floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Chubb is a British brand of door lock and safe; 'bottomless' drops its final B.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

definitions.meaning: in cricket six deliveries make an over
struck with sudden love or amazement

explanation.surface: A cricketer completes his set of deliveries and is besotted.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowler who has delivered six balls has bowled an over, and someone smitten with love is overwhelmed by it.

parts.note: the Magi are the three wise men of the Nativity
not is a negative word

explanation.surface: Sages give a negative answer about a line of defence.
explanation.walkthrough: The French built a line of forts along the German border in the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maginot Line was France's chain of fortifications on its eastern frontier.

clue.text: Important doctor taking people to America

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
men stands for people

explanation.surface: A significant physician brings people over to the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Something momentous is of great consequence or significance.

definitions.meaning: a person who disparages or finds fault
the fitting rapped by visitors on a front door

explanation.surface: A hostile reviewer standing at the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: A knocker is one who runs others down, and the metal ring or hammer on a front door is a knocker.

clue.text: Ken, monarch at present on the shelf

parts.note: K, king, is a monarch
now means at present
a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A man named Ken and a king are currently left unwanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' looks like a name but is the noun meaning range of understanding, as in 'beyond my ken'. 'on the shelf' hides the piece shelf with 'on the' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One's ken is the range of one's understanding or what one knows.

clue.text: Crowd round back end can be surprisingly methodical

indicators.note: round signals one word going around another

parts.note: a mass is a crowd

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word end from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mob gathers round the rear, yet behaves with unexpected order.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Hamlet: 'Though this be madness, yet there is method in't', so it can be surprisingly methodical.
explanation.definitionFit: Polonius remarks that Hamlet's apparent insanity has method in it, so lunacy can be orderly.

clue.text: Football team's turned up ' for cup games — they were swinging

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a football team, plus the S from the possessive
matches in a cup competition are ties

explanation.surface: A football side arrives for knockout matches in a swinging era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses XIS to SIX. In British football a cup match is called a tie. The decade is remembered as the Swinging Sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s are known as the swinging decade for their fashion, music and freedom.

clue.text: Unfinished account for dues makes one irritable

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a bill is an account to be paid
IOUs are written promises of money due

explanation.surface: Unpaid bills for outstanding debts leave a person bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the last L of BILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilious once meant full of bile, hence peevish and bad-tempered.

explanation.surface: Explosives set off, as if bursting a balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blasted with explosives has been destroyed in a blast, and a balloon filled with air has been inflated.

clue.text: A lot of digits are anaesthetised

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word is kept

parts.note: digits are numbers

explanation.surface: Many fingers and toes have lost feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' keeps most of NUMBERS, dropping ERS. 'digits' suggests fingers and toes, but means figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaesthesia deadens sensation, leaving the part without feeling.

definitions.meaning: public-school usage names the older of two boys as Smith ...
an army ... insignia is a crown

explanation.surface: The older brother becomes king.
explanation.walkthrough: At British private schools brothers are told apart as major and minor.
explanation.definitionFit: At British schools the elder of two brothers is called major, and a British Army major wears a crown as his rank badge.

parts.note: Oxford's sporting colour is a darker blue than Cambridge's, and a university athlete awarded colours is a blue

explanation.surface: A student athlete with a deeper complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete who represents Oxford earns a blue, and Oxford's shade is the darker one.

definitions.meaning: from Scotland, in the north of Britain

explanation.surface: A levy on northern Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Scotland, the northern part of Britain, and scot, an old levy, as in scot-free.

clue.text: Thing I take on as a protest

parts.note: an object is a thing

explanation.surface: Something I take on board as a form of complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: An objection is a statement of disapproval or dissent.

clue.text: Against one coming to God, classically, on TV

parts.note: V, versus, means against
I is the Roman numeral one
Deo is Latin for to or with God

explanation.surface: Opposing a person who turns to God on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classically' signals Latin: DEO is the form of deus used in phrases like 'Deo gratias'.
explanation.definitionFit: Video is recorded moving pictures shown on a television screen.

definitions.meaning: a bar or brace bearing a load
points to the swaggering walk of a proud person, the noun for that gait

explanation.surface: A prop for someone who walks with swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a brace holding up a structure, and strut is the swaggering gait of someone who walks proudly.
